text:
ana: Quick one 1: AP team in EMEA had a public holiday moved and a senior IC on a dependent visa had booked a floating day on the original date. Manager asked if we can carry that floating day to next FY since visa requires family travel in June. Thoughts?

peter: Short: country matters. If employee is UK-based, statutory leave rules apply; floats are company policy so we can be flexible, but must document and keep parity.

yun: Employee is UK, booked 1 floating day for 2026-12-24 (company moved observed holiday to 12/23). They can't travel earlier due to dependent school schedule. Manager proposes carryover of 8h into next FY.

people-ops-bot: people-ops-bot: Reminder: float-swap/carryover requests need: employee_id, country, original_date, requested_action, manager_signoff, reason. Use /forms/hr/float-exception.

ana: ana: Thanks. Two immediate flags: 1) if carryover pushes them above 40h cap, it needs People Ops director approval; 2) in UK, you can't enforce an expiry shorter than statutory minimum without legal sign-off.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Payroll note 1: if approved, we need a CSV with action codes and effective date before the payroll cutoff. Current cutoff for the cycle is 2026-04-08 17:00 GMT. If after cutoff, effective date will be next pay period. Example CSV: ```
employee_id,action,hours,effective_date,pay_code,notes
55433,carryover_add,8,2026-04-09,CARRY,visa exception
```

peter: Legal question: are we comfortable with a carryover that has a use-by date beyond statutory minimum? Legal should confirm whether UK allows conditional expiries for employer-discretion floats.

legal: legal: We need to review. In UK law, statutory holiday can't be detracted, but employer-designated floats can be subject to policy. However, for visa-dependent cases, discrimination risk is low but document reasons carefully. I'll review and confirm whether a 9-month use-by is enforceable.

yun: Manager suggests 9 months use-by and requires manager approval for any blackout weeks. They also request that the carried day be flagged so payroll doesn't auto-payout at termination.

ana: People Ops: that sounds reasonable. We'll require manager sign-off and add a note preventing payout on termination unless exception is approved. Also mark in HR tracker.

people-ops-bot: people-ops-bot: Checklist updated: add fields -> payout_on_termination (yes/no), use_by_date, manager_approval_required, coverage_plan. See /docs/hr/holiday-exceptions-checklist.md

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: If you want to prevent auto-payout at termination, set pay_code=NO_PAYOUT and payroll will honor it until system changeover. CSV example with flags: ```
employee_id,action,hours,effective_date,use_by_date,pay_code,no_payout,notes
55433,carryover_add,8,2026-04-09,2027-01-09,CARRY,TRUE,visa exception
```

peter: Legal: also confirm whether visa holder's dependent status affects statutory leave entitlements; if so, we might need to liaise with immigration counsel.

legal: noted. I'll loop in immigration-legal and get back in 48 hours.

yun: Manager will fill the float-exception form now and attach the travel docs (employee consented).

ana: Action items: yun to submit form + attach docs; legal to confirm UK enforceability and immigration impact; payroll to confirm CSV ingestion and lock the no-payout flag; People Ops to log exception and route to Director if cap exceeded. I'll ping Director if needed.

yun: Submitted the form and @mentioned @ana. Attached consent.

payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Received notification. If People Ops approves today, payroll can ingest CSV before cutoff. If Director sign-off needed, it'll shift to next cycle.

ana: Thanks. If Director approval is required I'll escalate. Otherwise we'll process as carryover with 9-month use-by and no-payout on termination.

peter: :thumbsup: Keep thread updated.

people-ops-bot: people-ops-bot: Closing checklist for this thread once all confirmations received.
